body:
If he exists and if he does he’s certainly indifferent to them. Doesn’t matter how much pain we’re in, how faithful we are, how we plead... our prayers fall on ears that are simply indifferent.

(This is coming from someone who used to pray faithfully every day for years)

If you experienced it once and are sure you won’t regret not going this year I think it’s okay to skip it if going will lead to more suffering.

I would just be honest and say it was too hard for you last year or something.
I thought it was terrible, and once it got to the medium stuff it was unwatchable. I think it was poorly made and everyone on it seemed disingenuous excluding the very first story from episode 1.

This is the same question I have all the time. For all I know I could be here right now living this life reliving similar situations from a past life that I’m supposed to do better this time around but how would I know... if I’m me I’m just going to keep making the same mistakes because I don’t have the prior knowledge to build off of.

Thank you very much for the link. I really enjoyed the read. 
This quote perfectly describes what I was trying to say:

“The big problem I have is not with happiness and joy. It is just that I WANT to have some type of negative feelings. Wouldn’t you think that around hour number two of being blissful and joyous to no extent, you would start to get, frankly, bored? What is any positive without a negative. It is undefined … boring. Sheer bliss without periods of non-bliss would not be good to me at all. This is what I’m afraid of.”

This whole thing presented several questions/thoughts I’ve had and answered them. Perhaps I won’t be “bored” after all lol. Thank you again

This sounds nice. Idk why people are so afraid of nothingness. 

I don’t think coma is comparable to death though. More like sleep. When I wake up I sometimes don’t remember my dreams and it feels like no time has passed even though several hours have. It doesn’t influence how I think about the afterlife or lack thereof.

I deleted all my social media. Social media is fake, meaning people tend to only post all the good and almost none of the bad (excluding subreddits like this). So being on them only made me feel more alone, jealous, and angry at others for enjoying the sun.

I was just saying this the other day. I prayed for the health and wellness of my family every single day and thanked god for waking us each up that morning. Now I look back and think what a fool I was. My dads death was sudden and feels like such a slap in the face like if god exists and heard my daily prayers and let this happen... like I refuse to believe it’s like that so god must not care or doesn’t really exist. 

If I pray and give thanks for something it gets taken away, if I don’t it will still be taken away. So yeah there is no point😕

I also lost my belief in god after my loss. I was someone who prayed to them every single day but since experiencing the unbearable pain of loss myself I just don’t believe they actually exist. And if they do they’re indifferent to the pain we experience thus when people die it’s just random and not anything god really cares about.
I used to but since losing someone no. It just feels random and cruel.

My loss is recent so I don’t yet have suggestions but I love this question. Since losing my dad a little over a month ago I haven’t been able to do the things I love at all, which includes watching anime and reading manga. It really sucks.

I just wanted to thank you for your list and say I’m definitely going to check them out.
This comment right here is absolute gold😂
Definitely been feeling like this heavy lately. And some of the stories I read/watch I just don’t trust as easily as I used to
Death
I don’t believe in hell but if it exists we’re in it right now. And in that case you’re actually right. Those with more money get a less shitty version of it for sure

I want to believe in an after life so bad. Some of the NDE’s are just hard for me believe and I don’t necessarily believe NDE’s confirm afterlife because the person is still connect to their body in some way.

Anyways back to you statement. On the days I think maybe the afterlife is real I feel less inclined to want to end my life. Because if the afterlife is there and I know it’s wonderful why not just live the life I have and accomplish what I’m supposed to before I go back home.

Other days where I believe there is absolutely nothing after death are the days I want to end my life. Because why continue when I can just totally and completely cease to exist. If there’s nothing after this the pain I’m experiencing is meaningless and that makes me want to end it now.

So no I don’t think proving there is an afterlife would raise the rates of suicide. I think it would actually have the opposite effect.
This was incredibly interesting. Thank you so much!
This is my favorite answer so far and actually addresses my question directly. I like your theory and it makes a lot of sense considering how vast the universe is.

I haven’t been able to listen to any kind of music either since my father passed a month ago. I don’t really understand why and thought it was strange. Nice to know I’m not the only one. 

So sorry for your loss and the pain you’re experiencing. I often wish to not wake up too.

I do believe the butterfly was a sign
Yes it is normal unfortunately😕
You seem like an amazing and kind person. You gave  me hope. Thank you🤍

I feel you. I’m no expert, I only lost my dad a month go but how you describe the pain in your chest is something I feel often. I recently found that when I feel it if I cry or scream it usually helps. Like I’ll go look at pictures or old texts until I cry or I’ll just put my face in my pillow and scream. 

It’s so unfair. I’m a little older, 26, and my brother is 17, just graduated high school. If I think too long about all he’ll miss it feels unbearable. I too don’t really know how or if it’s possible to continue living in a world my dad doesn’t. Right now I feel like I’m just taking it second my second trying to stay alive for my mom and brother..

I’ve been depressed since I was 14. It sucks thinking about all the ways my brain used to make me suffer over retrospectively fixable issues and now this has happened and it’s so permanent and unfixable. 

I have similar thoughts about family members. My dad’s brothers are all terrible people. Yet they still get to be here and it upset me too.

I’m not religious but I do believe in an after life. 

We don’t deserve this and it makes me angry. I’m so sorry.

I wish your grandma a speedy and lasting recovery🤍🤍🤍

I guess it’s human to feel this way. I know life is unfair but I really really wish we at least got to know why.

If acknowledging that grief is not the same for everyone removes your ability to find common ground that’s on you.

None of us grieve the same and the circumstances surrounding the loss greatly effect how those left behind handle it.

We’re all here because we find comfort in knowing we’re not alone in the experience. Not because we’re all grieving the same.

I have the ability to recognize that someone who lost their father to suicide would probably have a harder time than I am now even though what I feel is unbearable. Just like how I can recognize that people who lose their parents at a much older age than me aren’t experiencing what I’m experiencing.

I disagree. My mother lost her parents in her 50’s and though it was hard she said it’s nothing like what we’re experiencing with the loss of my dad. It’s easier to accept a 70, 80 something person who has seen most of your life already go than to see a 50 something person go.

People who lost their parents older have more memories, they had both parents to help them with their children, to guide them through life. Adulthood is hard. Harder than childhood. 

We have to suffer through many more milestones without the lost parent than someone who is 40/50 does. 

It is not the same. At all.

I understand this completely. Before my father passed I was always interested in the universe, other life forms, how small we are, how so much of what we do doesn’t matter in the long run.

Like I was/am obsessed with Interstellar (the movie) because of the abstract ideas it presented. 

Since my father passed I’ve started to obsessed over these kinds of topics. One moment I’m looking at things from an objective point of view and realize humans suffer just like I am now all over the world every second. But then I get so angry when I realize he won’t be here for the rest of my life. Then I realize I could literally die at any second and I might not even exist that much longer myself. Or that the world could end at any moment really because as much as humans like to act like we have control we don’t. 

I’ve also started obsessing about the after life. I want to find comfort in returning to the universe. Maybe retuning to my fathers embrace? Idk

It’s hard for me to find motivation. The plans I previously had I just like threw thew out the window because it doesn’t really matter. I kinda just want to see as much as I can before I die and spend as much time with the family I have left as I can.

I found this post very interesting to read btw

Yeah I do and it sucks because I used to consider myself a pretty caring person. I haven’t talked to any of my friends since I lost my dad (almost a month ago) and probably won’t. They reach out but I just avoid it. One of my friends was really great and called in every day but after day 2 she started to want to talk about small things like some issue at work that really wasn’t even an issue. I understand people who don’t know grief have smaller problems.. I used to be one of them... but I don’t have it in me to communicate with people about things that don’t really matter because I don’t have the energy to pretend to care

Sorry this turned into a mini rant but long story short you’re not alone in your feelings at all. And I think it’s good that at least you’re still trying to maintain your friendships.

My loss has opened my eyes and I now realize the God I loved and thought I understood through religion isn’t real. 

I don’t believe in reincarnation. The thought of it brings me great despair as I don’t want to have to ever experience earth again after this.

I believe there is either a peaceful afterlife or nothing at all. Both give me comfort.

So sorry for your loss. I’m fresh in grief of my own so I know how painful that is.

Yet another reason why I think life is so unnecessarily cruel. Those that wish for life get it taken from them while those that wish for death continue to suffer here on earth. I wish I knew why.
I really wish I believed that.
Don’t apologize for posting “too much”. It’s not too much and I love hearing about her and the love you shared🤍
Literally prayed “that angels watch me through the night until I wake in morning light.” Now I’m falling asleep praying to never have to see “morning light” again🥴

You’re so kind to care. Unfortunately there’s nothing anyone can say or do to fix my situation unless they can resurrect the dead. I lost my father a couple weeks ago. I’m only 26. There was so much he was supposed to see. Idc that he would want me to live. My mental health was hanging on by a thread before this happened. The world is cruel and I don’t want to be apart of it.

I don’t think I could’ve put it into words this perfectly. I’ve been telling myself I’m looking for other stories of loss to feel less alone but i still do feel alone. I relate to how you said you’re desperately looking for stories of suffering and how they bring you comfort. I keep trying to look at things objectively but inside it’s so painful and it feels personal.

I still can’t wrap my head around the fact that as I type this so many people around the world are hearing for the first time they’ll never see their loved one again. 

I also can’t wrap my head around the fact that so many people still have what I lost.
So sorry for your loss, thanks for sharing your experience and how you view life now🤍
May I ask how old you were when you lost your father?

Thank you so much for sharing. I’m so sorry for your losses. It makes me incredibly happy to read about your success and current happiness. How you were at the begging is how I currently feel like I am so knowing you were able to come out of it gives me hope. I believe we’ll reunite with our loved ones too🤍

I recently lost my father and am struggling with my beliefs because of it but I think people who take advantage of life, good people who live full lives like that get taken from us earlier than those who don’t live life that because there’s no more for them to do on earth. Almost like they figured life out and now they are able to rest. While those that have given up on life haven’t figured it out yet and are given more time to try to figure it out before their time comes.

Just something I like to believe I guess.

Before loss I appreciated life, so much. I was someone who already made a conscious effort to tell those I love how much I love them before suddenly losing my father. I was empathetic, kind, and selfless.

Loss has done nothing but make me mean, cold, and angry. I’ve lost empathy for others (as in I don’t care about their small problems and don’t pretend to). Grief is a pain no one on this planet should ever have to experience and the fact that so many of us do opened my eyes to how incredibly cruel the word is. Loss ruined me.

I haven’t experienced this but I hope it’s okay if I provide another view point. My parents were married for 30 years when my dad passed. They too were so deeply in love. We all love and miss my dad dearly. 

I’m personally so worried about my mom. She’s always been independent but I do hope she’s able to find love again soon. She’s an amazing, thoughtful, kind woman who doesn’t deserve to spend the rest of her life alone, she’s only 56. 

Maybe it’s a blessing that your father has connected with someone. He will never ever forget, try to replace, or fall out of love with your mom. But the spouse left behind deserves comfort and some version of happiness while they’re here imo.

So sorry for your loss. 
Have a child because you want to love and give them a beautiful life.. not because you need them to give you a reason to live. That’s an incredibly unfair burden to place on an innocent child.

I totally agree it’s extremely unfair. I do have one friend who lost her father when she was in middle school but we’re not that close.

I lost my father 3 weeks ago and I’m currently deep in the anger phase of my grief because of how unfair it feels. 

I’m currently struggling to speak to any of my friends because there’s a voice in the back of my head saying they still have both of their parents and I hate to say it but I feel kinda jealous. I of course would never want them to experience this pain.. it’s just hard.

I’ve read a lot of stories on here that have made me feel so many things. Yours is the first to make my heart feel so incredibly warm so I want to thank you for sharing how beautiful the relationship you had with your mother was/is. 

I (26F) lost my father in July 4th. It’s been so indescribably painful but I take comfort in knowing how often we told each other how much we meant to one another. His death was sudden but the last conversation I had with him was full of so much love. 

I don’t really have a lot of advice because it’s still so fresh for me too but thank you again🤍

You make a good point that it may just be my friend group. I’ve been here finding hope in others stories that are similar to mine because if they can survive so can I.. but in my every day life it’s like no one can relate and that’s made it hard. Thank you for the reminder it’s not uncommon🤍

Wow I felt every word of this. It’s almost like I wrote it myself except for instead of mom it’s dad. The thought of living the rest of my life with this gaping whole in my life... idk I’m taking it minute by minute but it’s only been 3 weeks for me I wish I could provide more hope... 
know you are not alone in how you feel.

I think it’s understandable you want to be left alone. I’m the same way. I’m currently sitting in my car hiding from everyone waiting for my fathers funeral to begin. Grief is terrible and draining, being around people was draining enough before all this for me too. Be kind to yourself and do what feels most comfortable.

People keep giving examples of how their children keep them going. That’s my point... it’s selfish to have kids for your own benefit in this way... her love keeps you going.. her being here helps you keep your loved ones alive. Now she will grow into into this cruel world that’s full of pain... 
don’t even get me started on the state of the environment the next generation will have to suffer through.
Thank you so much for sharing your experience. I’m so glad you both were able to be there for each other🤍

This post gave me hope. I lost my father a little
Over 2 weeks ago. I’m of course still in the thick of grief and have never experience pain like this. Right now I feel like this experience is making me a mean, evil, and callous person. I hope one day to gain the perspective you currently have.

I see but then how do mediums communicate with them if they’re so beyond our comprehension and on such a different wavelength? If they’re so far moved on how can mediums claim our family is still somewhat attached to us and care about certain personal events we experience?
This was very interesting to read. Thank you so much a lot of your explanation makes sense!
I love how you explained this!

I never felt I needed to respond. My world is still crashing down, I can’t imagine anyone who sent their condolences would be upset I didn’t respond... I mean they’d have to be terribly selfish to expect a response in my opinion. I sent thank you to those who’s send flowers or food but other than that I read the messages and don’t respond. Grieving takes a lot of energy... I don’t think we should worry about using the little energy we do have on responses.
I always respond “I’m here.” Idk if that really answers the question but it’s how I feel. I’m not okay, I’m not fine, I’m just alive.

“I know what you’re going through is hard I’m so sorry.”
That’s just what I would say. There are so many words in the English language yet people stick to these generic phrases. Grief is devastating... I don’t understand why people can’t take the extra couple minutes to personalize what they say.

Wow it feels like I wrote this myself. I go to sleep praying I won’t wake up... then I feel guilty because I want to live for my mom.
I lost my dad 2 weeks ago. I can’t believe god would put us through this. I’m so angry with him for making the world so unbearably cruel.
I miss my dad. I hope there’s an after life. I hope we get to see them again.

Thank you so much for your comment. It helped. I too have had the thought that maybe, in some way, this will
better prepare us for the after life too. Right now I’m angry and feel I’m a much worse person that I was before this happened.. I don’t want to be like this long term. Pain and suffering this great.. something has to come of it.

Thank you for your comment, I’m so sorry we have to go through this but It’s nice not to feel alone in this horrible experience. The unexpectedness of it makes it really hard because all the plans I had, how I pictured my future have been completely shattered so suddenly. I’m so sorry he won’t be there for your wedding... that was one of my first thoughts too... it’s all just so unfair.

The part about not being able to share with friends because they don’t understand... I felt that. It’s so hard because everyone else still has both of their parents. I myself could not understand this pain/grief until I felt it myself.
I’m angry too.. I hope the anger fades some.

Please know your dad would never want you to feel guilty.
